en.title: Most Drop Points Covered by One Horizontal or Vertical Flight Line
en.description:
Choose one horizontal or vertical straight line; directions cannot be mixed, and diagonal lines cannot be chosen. The line must cover at least two input points; output the maximum number of points covered, or 0 if this is impossible. Duplicate coordinates are counted as many times as they are recorded in the input.

See the input protocol for this site's supplements to missing ranges and its recovery of typos in the source.
en.input: The input is n, then n x-coordinates and n y-coordinates. The original bound 2≤n≤700 is recovered from the complete supplementary raw; coordinates have no original numeric bound, and this site adds −10^9..10^9. The truncated main raw is recovered from a complete raw of the same problem; another version with a diagonal example 5 conflicts with its own rules and is not adopted.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 3; 0; 2. Verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Count the occurrences of each x-coordinate and each y-coordinate separately, take the maximum, and handle the condition of covering at least two points.
